title: Transportation Authority design contracts that grew by amendment
question: Do Transportation Authority professional contracts start small and grow by later amendments?
finding: Three design contracts with WMH Corporation started at $5.5 million together and stand at $25.0 million after the amendments the memos ask for: the west-side bridges contract went from $1.6 million in 2010 to $17.8 million in 2023 (11.11 times), Hillcrest Road from $2.7 million to $3.8 million, and the island path from $1.1 million to $3.4 million within two years. The bridges construction-management contract with WSP doubled, $5.5 million to $11.5 million. WMH was also the higher-ranked of two proposers for the 2021 freeway managed-lanes study, and the island path design drew two proposals.
how: First award and latest amount as stated in the history paragraphs of the 2023, 2024 and 2026 board memos.
limits: The bridges contract was let in three phases with the option to amend for each written into the original request, and the memos attribute much of the growth to a re-scoping when Caltrans changed the funding plan and to a longer construction period; phased amendments are permitted and approved by the Board. What is missing is a record of whether the later phases were ever priced competitively.
